name: Morning banana diet

lead: The morning banana diet has people eat raw bananas with room-temperature water at breakfast, then eat normal meals at lunch and dinner until about 80 percent full, with dinner early in the evening and no late snacking.
Its payoff is gradual fat loss, which gives a leaner face and body. It began in Japan in 2008, spread through television and caused banana shortages, and returned on social media around 2023.

paras: Bananas on waking, only room-temperature water, regular lunch and early dinner, no desserts or alcohol after dinner and one optional afternoon snack. Followers report results over months.

Dietitians cited in coverage say that any loss comes from lower calorie intake, not bananas themselves. Bananas contain little protein and the routine can be repetitive; people with diabetes or kidney disease are advised to be careful.

chain: Fat loss, leaner face and waist
angle.text: People follow it to lose weight steadily, which makes the face and midsection look leaner. The structure is a routine with few rules and no calorie counting.

lead: The morning banana diet, called the Asa banana diet in Japan, was devised in 2008 by Osaka pharmacist Sumiko Watanabe for her husband Hitoshi, who reportedly lost about 17 kg after adopting banana breakfasts [1]. It is used for weight loss, which many people pursue as part of a leaner appearance.

The rules are simple: raw, room-temperature bananas and water at breakfast, normal meals eaten to about 80 percent fullness, no eating after 8 p.m., and no desserts or alcohol after dinner [1]. It spread via the social network Mixi and television, where singer Kumiko Mori described losing about 7 kg, and a book on the diet sold more than 730,000 copies by October 2008 [1]. Banana sales rose sharply and shortages followed [1]. The diet resurged on TikTok around 2023 [1].

paras: Breakfast is one or more raw bananas at room temperature with room-temperature water. Lunch and dinner are freely chosen, eaten until about 80 percent full, with dinner finished by about 8 p.m., ideally earlier. Desserts and alcohol after dinner are excluded, with one afternoon snack allowed [1].

After Hitoshi Watanabe's reported loss, the diet was shared on Mixi and then promoted on television in 2008, and a banana shortage was reported across Japan in the autumn [1]. Proponents credit the fibre of bananas for fullness, and the early cutoff for fewer calories [1].

The Grokipedia summary states that formal research is limited and that dietitians attribute any loss to reduced calories and portion control rather than a unique effect of bananas [1]. It also lists possible issues: low protein, bloating for some people, and care for diabetes or kidney disease [1].

lore.intro: Followers report losing several kilograms over months.

claims.claim: Bananas for breakfast cause weight loss

timeline.event: Diet devised by Sumiko Watanabe; spreads in Japan; bananas short in stores [1]
